questions.q: What does an Approval Step's Step Criteria control?
options: Whether all records reaching the step enter it, or only ones matching a condition
Which users can view the approval process definition
How many email templates the step can use
The object the approval process is defined on
questions.explain: Step Criteria lets a step be conditional, for example only discounts over 20% continue to a VP step, which is what makes multi-step routing possible.

questions.q: Why assign an approval step to a Queue instead of a specific named user?
options: Queues respond to approval requests automatically with no human action
Queues are required for parallel approval to work at all
It avoids hard-coding one person's name, so the process keeps working as team membership changes
It removes the need for an email notification template
questions.explain: A queue is a group of users who share responsibility; any member can act, so the process doesn't break when one person is out or leaves the team.

questions.q: What distinguishes a parallel approval from a serial (multi-step) one?
options: Parallel approval can only be used with Queues
Parallel means multiple approvers assigned within the same step, responding independently
Serial approval can only have one approval step total
Parallel approval has no entry criteria at all
questions.explain: Serial is step after step, different people in sequence. Parallel is multiple approvers on one step at the same time.

questions.q: Can serial and parallel approval be combined in a single approval process?
options: Only when using the Jump Start Wizard
Only if the process has exactly two steps
No, a process must be entirely serial or entirely parallel
Yes, for example unanimous parallel approval within Step 1, followed by a single serial approver in Step 2
questions.explain: A step can have multiple parallel approvers, and a process can have multiple steps in sequence, so the two combine naturally in real-world processes.

questions.q: In a parallel step set to "require unanimous approval," what happens if one of two assigned approvers rejects the record?
options: The step is rejected immediately; the second approver's response doesn't matter
The record is deleted
The step is approved anyway once the second approver responds
The process restarts from Step 1
questions.explain: Unanimous approval requires every assigned approver to approve. A single rejection stops the step regardless of what the other approver would have said.
